t.checkSub: Paste an SMS, WhatsApp, email or call script. Everything is checked on your phone and nothing is uploaded.
t.checkSample: [Bank Security] Dear customer, your bank account has been suspended due to suspicious activity. To avoid permanent closure, verify your identity within 24 hours at bit.ly/bank-verify-now and enter the OTP sent to you. Do not share this with anyone.
t.checkEmpty: Paste a message above to check it.
t.adviceHigh: Don't reply, click links or send money. Block the sender and contact your bank or the police if you're unsure.
t.adviceMid: Check with the organisation using a number you find yourself, not one in the message.
t.adviceLow: This doesn't match common scam patterns, but scammers change tactics. If money or codes are involved, check first.
t.r0t: Asks for an OTP, PIN or password
t.r0d: No bank, government agency or delivery company will ever ask for your OTP.
t.r1t: Pretends to be government or police
t.r1d: Scammers often pose as the police, tax office, immigration, central bank, customs or a court. Real officers won't ask you to transfer money.
t.r2d: Pressure to act 'now' stops you from thinking or checking.
t.r3d: Requests to transfer money, especially to a 'safe account', are a hallmark of scams.
t.r4d: Gift cards, crypto and prepaid vouchers can't be traced or reversed.
t.r5t: Contains a link or shortened URL
t.r5d: Don't tap links in unexpected messages. Short links hide where they really go.
t.r6t: Asks you to install an app or share your screen
t.r6d: Remote-access apps let scammers control your phone and bank apps.
t.r7d: Unexpected prizes, refunds or lucky draws are bait.
t.r8d: Easy money for liking videos, 'tasks' or guaranteed returns is a common scam.
t.r9t: Asks you to keep it secret
t.r9d: Scammers tell you not to talk to family or the bank so no one can warn you.
t.r10t: Asks you to confirm personal or bank details
t.r10d: Real organisations already have your details and won't ask by message.
t.r11d: Fake 'failed delivery' notices lead to phishing pages.
t.r12d: Messages from unfamiliar international numbers, or recorded voice calls asking you to press a key, need extra care.
t.r13d: A friend or relative suddenly needing money, or fast romance, is a common setup.

t.tip1: Call your bank's 24-hour hotline right away to freeze your account and cards.
t.tip2: Stop all contact with the scammer. Don't send any more money or codes.
t.tipReportSG: Report it to the police at 1800 255 0000 or online at police.gov.sg/i-witness, and ask for a report number for your bank.
t.tipReport: Report it to the police in {country} and ask for a report number for your bank.
t.tipReportNum: Report it to the police in {country} ({num}) and ask for a report number for your bank.
t.tip4: Keep screenshots of chats, phone numbers and transaction records.
t.tip5: Uninstall any app the caller asked you to install (e.g. AnyDesk, TeamViewer).
t.numbersChange: Numbers can change. Confirm local emergency numbers with your hotel or your country's embassy when you arrive.

t.msg_danger: 🚨 SOS – I'm in danger or feel unsafe. Please call me now. If I don't answer, call the local police and give them my location below.
t.msg_scam: 🚨 SOS – A scam is happening right now. Someone may be pressuring me to send money, codes or personal details. Please call me straight away and stop me from paying or sharing anything. Don't send money to anyone who asks on my behalf.
t.msg_kidnap: 🚨 SOS – I've been taken or I'm being held against my will. Call the police now and give them my location below. Don't call or message me, as it may not be safe. Don't pay anyone who asks for money; tell the police instead.
t.msg_medical: 🚨 SOS – Medical emergency. I need urgent medical help. Please call me. If I don't answer, call the local ambulance and give them my location below.
t.msg_accident: 🚨 SOS – I've been in an accident. Please call me. If I don't answer, call the local emergency number and give them my location below.
t.msg_evac: 🚨 SOS – I need to get to safety. Please call me and help me find a safe way out. My location is below.
t.notePh: e.g. I'm travelling with Aunty Lim. Blood type O+.
